methodologyNotes: Roster covers twelve home elliptical trainers (rear-drive, front-drive, and center-drive) spanning the $179-$4,199 price range, including current models, recently replaced models, and one discontinued model still widely searched. Primary sources are manufacturer product pages (NordicTrack, Schwinn, Sole, Bowflex, Horizon, ProForm, Sunny Health) and high-authority review sites (BarBend, Treadmill Review Guru, Treadmill Doctor, The Fit House, Garage Gym Reviews, FitRated). Prices are published US MSRPs or typical current retail prices as of the access date; discontinued models retain last-known/last-verified MSRP noted explicitly. Adversarial re-verification (2026-06-19) corrected the Precor EFX 245 price (3499->4199 per Treadmill Doctor) and Schwinn 470 drive type (rear->front per multiple sources), and nulled the EFX 245 release year. resistance_levels and built_in_programs are integer counts; flywheel_lb and max_user_weight_lb are numbers; stride_length_in is a string carrying units when the stride is a range. accessedAt 2026-06-19.

products.name: NordicTrack AirGlide 14i
products.priceNote: MSRP; direct replacement for the discontinued Commercial 14.9
products.provenance: BarBend review (verified live, by Rosie Borchert NASM-CPT) confirms $1,799, 32 lb flywheel, 26 resistance levels, -5 to 15% power incline, 300 lb capacity, 17.8-18.5 in auto-adjusting stride, and front-drive design (flywheel housed at the front). Standalone preset program count is not published (iFIT manual mode only without subscription), so built_in_programs is null.

products.name: NordicTrack Commercial 14.9
products.priceNote: Last-known MSRP (~$1,799-1,999); discontinued mid-2023, replaced by AirGlide 14i
products.provenance: The Fit House (verified live) and Treadmill Review Guru confirm front-drive, 17.5-18.7 in auto-adjustable stride, 32 lb flywheel, 26 resistance levels, 0-20% power incline, 350 lb capacity, and 35 built-in programs. Last-known MSRP just under $1,800 (table also shows $1,999). Discontinued mid-2023; succeeded by the AirGlide 14i.

products.name: NordicTrack FS14i FreeStride Trainer
products.priceNote: MSRP per NordicTrack.com and Treadmill Review Guru
products.provenance: Treadmill Review Guru (verified live) confirms center-drive (flywheel beside the pedals), up-to-32 in variable stride, 26 resistance levels, -10% to +10% power incline/decline, 375 lb capacity, 20 lb flywheel, and 2 onboard workout programs (machine is iFIT-centric). $2,499 MSRP. The FS14i functions as an elliptical, stepper, and running simulator.

products.name: Sole E35
products.priceNote: MSRP per Sole official site; marked sold out at time of access
products.provenance: Sole official product page (verified live) confirms $1,699.99, 25 lb flywheel, 20 resistance levels, 20 incline levels, 20-inch stride, 350 lb capacity, and 10 pre-programmed workouts. Front-drive design confirmed by Treadmill Doctor and FitRated. NOTE: FitRated/Treadmill Doctor cite 375 lb capacity for an earlier config; the manufacturer's current page states 350 lb, which is retained here as the primary source.

products.name: Sole E25
products.priceNote: MSRP per Sole official site; BarBend notes street price around $900
products.provenance: Sole official site (verified live) confirms $1,299.99 MSRP, 20 lb flywheel, 20 resistance levels, 20 incline levels, 350 lb capacity, and 7 pre-programmed + 2 user-defined workouts. BarBend (verified live) confirms front-drive, 20-inch stride, and counts 10 programmed workouts total (6 standard + 2 heart-rate + 2 custom); built_in_programs kept at 10 to match BarBend's explicit total. Program count is ambiguous between sources (manufacturer table implies 9).

products.name: Bowflex Max Trainer M9
products.provenance: Bowflex official page (verified live) shows $1,999 MSRP (on sale $1,799) and 20 resistance levels. Treadmill Doctor (verified live) confirms 300 lb capacity, 4 built-in programs, and no incline. The M9 uses combined magnetic and fan/air resistance rather than a traditional flywheel, so flywheel_lb is null. Stride length is not a fixed traditional measurement due to the hybrid elliptical-stepper motion; left null.

products.name: ProForm Carbon EL
products.priceNote: Typical current retail price; Scheels and 360 Fitness list at $799.99
products.provenance: Scheels retailer page (verified live) confirms $799.99, 19-inch MANUAL-adjustable stride, 18 resistance levels, 275 lb capacity, and 15 lb flywheel. Treadmill Doctor's claim of a 'power-adjustable' stride and 300 lb capacity is contradicted by the manufacturer-aligned retailer listing, so manual/275 lb is retained. Incline is a manual ramp, not motorized (power_incline false). Standalone preset programs are not listed (iFIT app content); built_in_programs null.

products.name: Horizon EX-59
products.priceNote: MSRP per Horizon Fitness / BarBend (frequently on sale ~$799)
products.provenance: BarBend (verified live, the cited corroboration) confirms $999.99 MSRP, 18-inch stride, 10 resistance levels, 14.3 lb flywheel, 300 lb capacity, 5 preset programs (Calorie, Distance, Intervals, Manual, Weight Loss), and no incline/decline. Garage Gym Reviews confirms $999 MSRP (sale ~$799). Front-drive ECB magnetic system. (Some third-party pages cite $699/10 programs, which reflect street price and/or a different model; BarBend primary corroboration retained.)

products.name: Schwinn 470
products.priceNote: Last-known MSRP; discontinued, replaced by Schwinn 490 (debuted Sept 2023)
products.provenance: CORRECTED drive type rear_drive->front_drive: Garage Gym Reviews, FitRated, and Sole's E25-vs-470 comparison all confirm the 470 is a FRONT-drive elliptical (flywheel positioned in front). Specs confirmed: 20-inch stride, 25 eddy-current resistance levels, 10-degree motorized incline, 300 lb capacity, 20 lb perimeter-weighted flywheel, 29 preset programs. Discontinued; Nautilus debuted the Schwinn 490 in Sept 2023 as its replacement (Amazon lists 470 as discontinued). Source URL switched to Garage Gym Reviews because Schwinn's own page now returns a discontinued/$0 listing.

products.name: Schwinn 411
products.priceNote: MSRP per Schwinn Fitness official site
products.provenance: Schwinn official product page (verified live) confirms $699, 18-inch stride, 16 magnetic resistance levels, 300 lb capacity, 13 workout programs, and explicitly 'No' incline. Flywheel weight is not published by Schwinn for this model (null). Front-drive confirmed by multiple review sources.

products.name: Precor EFX 245
products.priceNote: Last-verified MSRP per Treadmill Doctor; limited retail availability as of 2026; predates Precor's current EFX 500-800 home lineup
products.provenance: CORRECTED price 3499->4199: Treadmill Doctor (verified live, the cited source) lists $4,199, rear-drive, 18-21 inch adjustable stride, 16 resistance levels, motorized Precor CrossRamp (15-25 degrees / 8 levels), 275 lb tested capacity, and 40 total programs (24 preset + 16 custom). Flywheel weight not published by Precor (null). releaseDate nulled (draft hedged 'approximately 2019'; Energy Series launch year not confidently verifiable).

products.name: Sunny Health & Fitness SF-E905
products.priceNote: Typical Amazon/retail price (~$179-181); marked sold out on manufacturer site
products.provenance: Treadmill Doctor (verified live) confirms 11-inch stride, 8 magnetic resistance levels, 220 lb capacity, and ~$179-181 street price. Flywheel weight and built-in programs are not specified by the manufacturer (both null). Budget model with LCD monitor only; no incline.
